newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Lottery prizes entice Romanians to vote.
newsitem.headline: Lottery prizes entice Romanians to vote.

text.p: Romanians had reasons other than civic duty for voting in Sunday's presidential run-off election -- the chance to win $20,000 in a lottery.

The country's largest private television channel ProTV was offering two prizes of 100 million lei each to voters who sent in postcards forecasting the outcome of the contest between incumbent Ion Iliescu and academic Emil Constantinescu.
To claim their prize the winners had to produce a stamp from a polling station to prove they voted.
All 1.2 million cards were dumped into a new red cement mixer truck from which the winning entries were to be drawn.
Thousands of viewers queued outside the ProTV studios in the capital Bucharest for a chance at lesser prizes, which ranged from television sets to woollen hats.

Voters in the first round of voting earlier this month also took part in a state television lottery offering nine tractors to villages with the highest turnout in each of Romania's historic districts.
